title: Tasman Retail — inventory integration livestream notes
content:
Meeting: Tasman Retail technical livestream (60m) — initial integration capture
Date: 2026-02-24
Attendees: Asha (CS), Carlos (Solutions Eng), Priya (Tasman infra lead), Mark (Tasman app), Lina (product ops)
TL;DR: Tasman wants a low-latency SKU assistant for stores and web that uses embeddings for similar-SKU lookup + text generation for human-friendly result text. They prefer a Private deployment (VPC) with optional on-prem cache layer. Initial target: 100 QPS peak for search+rewrite path, p95 latency <= 220ms for single-turn SKU lookup.

Background/context:
- Tasman is a regional retail chain (450 stores) with an existing inventory microservice (REST) and nightly catalog sync.
- Current pain: poor search relevance across SKUs, SKU attribute sparsity, and mobile lookup latency spikes during promos.
- They want our inference layer to power: in-store clerk assistant, mobile search rewrite, and a daily re-ranking job for catalog freshness.

Core technical asks from Tasman:
- Embedding-based similarity endpoint to return top-K candidates from 100k SKU corpus in <150ms (including vector DB lookup).
- Text generation endpoint to synthesize short assistant replies (<= 40 tokens).
- Data residency: catalog + sales history must stay in their AWS account inside a private subnet (VPC).
- Auth: they will use vault-managed API keys and expect mutual TLS for control-plane comms.

Notes on constraints and environment:
- They want to run Redwood Private (control plane external, runtime within their VPC).
- Existing infra: EKS cluster in us-west-2, RDS Postgres for catalog, Redis for sessions (but small).
- They already trialed a managed vector DB (hosted) but are open to running an in-VPC Faiss/Annoy/Weaviate.
- Ops maturity: small infra team, prefers opinionated defaults and automated runbooks/alerts.

Immediate technical observations (gotchas / risks):
- Tokenization mismatch risk: Tasman product SKUs include special separators (e.g., "SKU-123/XL"). Need tokenizer sanity check for any gen model used for rewrites. Recommend run of 1000-sample tokenization audit.
- Vector DB cold-start: If they use an in-VPC vector DB, initial index build times could cause slow first queries; need caching and warmup strategy.
- Prefix caching: mobile flow expects near-instant responses when clerk enters partial SKU; recommend prefix/KV caching and a small LRU cache deployed close to app tier.
- Multi-modal catalog fields: images may be used later for similarity; design embeddings pipeline to add image vector placeholders now.
- Cost sensitivity: they flagged budget cap for first 6 months — propose mixed strategy: small-memory quantized model for generation + dedicated GPU pool scaled to schedule.

Proposed integration architecture (high level):
- Ingest: nightly catalog sync -> transform (normalize SKUs, text templates) -> compute embeddings (batch) -> upsert into in-VPC vector DB.
- Online path: App -> internal proxy -> Redwood runtime (in-VPC) -> either query vector DB (top-K) -> pass candidates + short prompt -> generate textual assistant reply.
- Fallback: if vector DB returns <N candidates -> run a looser retrieval with a sparse retriever or fallback to keyword search.

Quick wins we can offer (low lift):
- Run a 2-hour tokenization smoke test + 200 sample prompts to check hallucination and token lengths. (Carlos)
- Provide a sample ingestion script for embeddings using their nightly dump schema. (Asha)
- Recommend a 1-node Faiss helm chart and a 1 day warmup run using last-week sales as seed. (Eng template)

Action items / next steps:
- CS -> share sample catalog dump (CSV, anonymized) and an API key for staging (Tasman). Target: 2026-03-02. (Owner: Priya)
- Solutions Eng -> run tokenization and 200-prompt hallucination smoke test; deliver short report + suggested model variant (gpt-redwood-small, gpt-redwood-medium). Target: 2026-03-05. (Owner: Carlos)
- Infra (Tasman) + SRE -> validate VPC peering options and mTLS requirements; list any net egress constraints. Target: 2026-03-08. (Owner: Mark)
- Product -> prepare SLA/limit sheet for 100 QPS profile and cost estimate (monthly). Target: 2026-03-09. (Owner: Lina)
- Create Jira epic CS-4123 and link PR template for integration repo. (Asha)

Open questions (needs Tasman & Redwood decisions):
- Vector DB choice: will Tasman use hosted vendor or self-hosted in VPC? Cost comparison required.
- Do they need real-time catalog updates (sub-minute), or is nightly batch sufficient for initial phase?
- Sensitive attributes: which SKU fields are PII (if any) — need classification for KMS/HSM handling.
- Monitoring: what SLI thresholds beyond p95 latency (error budget, cold-start rate) matter to their ops team?

Potential technical experiments (for next call):
- A/B test: quantized generator vs full float model for p95 latency and customer satisfaction (via small prompt set).
- Embedding recall sweep: compare Open-source embeddings vs Redwood-verified embeddings on their SKU similarity metrics.
- Prefix cache TTL tuning: find sweet spot between staleness and hit-rate for peak hours.

Misc notes / conversation fragments:
- Priya: "We cannot expose any sales history outside our VPC, so if control plane needs telemetry we must anonymize at source."
- Mark: "Can we start with a read-only staging RDS replica for vector-upsert jobs?"
- Tasman concern about evaluation: they want an initial QA script that flags hallucinations on product attributes (price, size).

Decision points for next leadership sync:
- Approve Private deployment architecture and minimum dedicated capacity (1x A10x equivalent) for pilot.
- Agree on vector DB approach and whether Redwood will provide managed indexing automation on their VPC.

References / links from call:
- Tasman daily catalog sample (requested): share via secure transfer (SFTP) — action: Priya
- Related Redwood doc: confluence:tasman-inventory-arch-v1
- Jira: CS-4123 (epic) & INF-298 (infra investigation)

End notes: keep this as the working capture. Will convert to formal onboarding checklist once we have catalog dump and tokenization report.
summary: Working call notes for Tasman Retail SKU assistant pilot — capture requirements, constraints, initial architecture and action items.
